49/ 3/8/16
Shanghai Municipal Council.
August 2nd 1916

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL POLICE FORCE JUNCTA JUVANT）
POLICE FORCE,
(DETECTIVE BRANCH)

Sir,
A report has been made to this Department to the effect that the 15000 mauser rifles and the 500 rounds of ammunition, for each of which so much has been said, are the property of Arnhold Karberg & Co, that they are stored in a godown near the Settlement but not inside the boundary, that they have entrusted the sale to a Chinese upon condition that he sells only to another Chinese and not to a foreigner, that this man has found a buyer named Fong who alleges that he is a buyer for the Russian, that Fong insists on a $10,000 deposit in token of good faith, that he will deposit an equal amount, both sums to be placed in the Bank of the Netherlands Trading Society, that the seller is willing to make the deposit but insists that it shall be placed in the International Banking Corporation and that Fong declines to agree to this on the ground that the manager of the latter establishment is an American born in Germany. Fong has an European whom he knows and whom he is prepared to call upon to examine the weapons when their whereabouts is revealed; and the seller has also an European who is described as an ex employee of the Customs of Scandinavian or German nationality, wearing glasses, a blond moustache and closely cropped hair, will come forward and discuss matters with Fong's foreign representative when the deal is under way.
Between the two parties there is a cloud of Chinese brokers amongst whom are one or two Japanese. Some are intent on gaining commission from one side or the other, some from both, whilst others are eager to discover where the arms are stored in order that they may supply the information to the Custom Authorities and obtain from them a reward of 60 per cent of the value of the seizure.
The delivery will not be made in Shanghai but at Woosung to which place the arms will be taken in cargo boats towed by steam launches.

Your Obedient Servant,
[签名]
Chief Detective Inspector.

[手写批注：D.P ? / km 2/8 / Ash]
Captain Superintendent of Police.
pages.zh:
49/ 3/8/16
上海工部局。
1916年8月2日

（印章：上海工部局警务处 协力同心）
警务处，
（侦探股）

先生：

本部接获报告称，此前备受关注的15,000支毛瑟步枪及每支配备的500发子弹，系阿诺德·卡尔伯格公司（Arnhold Karberg & Co.）之财产；这批军火储存在租界附近但不在界线之内的一座仓库中；该公司已委托一名华人进行销售，条件是他只能卖给另一名华人，不得卖给外国人；该受托人已找到一位名为方（Fong）的买家，方声称自己是代表俄国人购买；方坚持要求支付10,000美元定金以示诚意，并表示他将存入同等金额，两笔款项均须存入荷兰贸易银行（Bank of the Netherlands Trading Society）；卖方愿意支付定金，但坚持必须存入国际汇兑银行（International Banking Corporation），而方拒绝同意此安排，理由是后一家机构的经理是一名生于德国的美国人。方有一位认识的欧洲人，他准备在武器下落揭晓时请此人前来查验武器；卖方也有一名欧洲人，据描述为前海关雇员，斯堪的纳维亚或德国籍，戴眼镜，留金色胡须，头发剪得很短，将在交易进行时出面与方的外国代表洽谈事宜。

双方之间有一群华人居间人，其中有一两名日本人。有些人一心只想从一方或另一方获取佣金，有些人则想从双方获利，还有些人急于查明军火储存地点，以便向海关当局提供情报，从而获得相当于查获价值60%的赏金。

交货地点不在上海，而在吴淞，军火将由汽艇拖曳的货船运往该地。

您顺从的仆人，
[签名]
总探长。

[手写批注：D.P ? / km 8月2日 / Ash]
警务处总监。
